name: Rikkei Finance SimplePriceOracle setOracleData access control
summary: SimplePriceOracle 0xd55f01b4b51b7f48912cd8ca3cdd8070a1a9dba5, the price oracle of the Rikkei Finance Cointroller, declares `function setOracleData(address rToken, oracleChainlink _oracle) external { oracleData[rToken] = _oracle; }` with no owner, admin, or any other caller restriction, so any address can repoint any market's feed. getUnderlyingPrice then reads decimals() and latestRoundData() straight from whatever contract that mapping holds. The attacker deposited 0.0001 BNB into rBNB, called setOracleData(rBNB, ownContract) to make the rBNB feed return 4.16881147930e32 with 18 decimals instead of the Chainlink BNB/USD 416.24753868 with 8 decimals, and borrowed the entire cash of the rUSDC, rBTC, rDAI, rUSDT and rBUSD markets against the resulting 2.918e28 account liquidity, then restored the original feed. A second transaction in the same block repeated the pattern in the opposite direction, repointing the rBNB feed at a second attacker contract so that BNB was priced low enough to borrow the whole rBNB market against a dust rBUSD deposit.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract created directly by an EOA. The address has no code at block 15341134 and its runtime code hash is 0xe57bae111f926347b290fa23499ce2258e3c04d6a7a4836d5fda47d2b7435510 at the creation block 15341135 and at blocks 16000000, 16500000 and 16956474; its EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots, EIP-1822 proxiable slot and OpenZeppelin legacy implementation slot all read zero at block 16956474, and it emitted no log at all between creation and the exploit block, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

The campaign is two transactions in block 16956475 from the same EOA: 0x93a9b022 at transaction index 3 emptied the rUSDC, rBTC, rDAI, rUSDT and rBUSD markets, and 0x4e067608 at transaction index 118 emptied the rBNB market. Each borrow requested exactly the market's getCash(), and every underlying balance confirms it: rUSDC 0x916e87d16b2f3e097b9a6375dc7393cf3b5c11f5 346199.780826500224370302 -> 0 USDC, rBTC 0x53abf990bf7a37faa783a75fdd75bbcf8bdf11eb 3.032997772596307847 -> 0 BTCB, rDAI 0x9b9006cb01b1f664ac25137d3a3a20b37d8bc078 52275.872910150015513225 -> 0 DAI, rUSDT 0x383598668c025be0798e90e7c5485ff18d311063 297082.798044846109795784 -> 0 USDT, rBUSD 0x6db6a55e57ac8c90477bbf00ce874b988666553a 299822.459019477022693829 -> 0.041669357174238900 BUSD (the attacker's own dust deposit), and rBNB 0x157822ac5fa0efe98daa4b0a55450f4a182c10ca 101.469592805999411776 -> 0 BNB, all measured between block 16956474 and 16956475. Nothing was repaid; the positions were left as bad debt against 0.0001 BNB and 0.041429023913104989 BUSD of attacker collateral. Binance-peg USDC, USDT, BUSD and DAI are valued at par; BTCB and BNB use the DefiLlama observations nearest the incident timestamp (40228.48815584733 at 1649992763 and 416.03796227746824 at 1649992784). The attacker converted the proceeds and moved 2673.2 BNB, about 1.11M USD at the same BNB price, into the Tornado Cash BNB pool 0x0d5550d52428e7e3175bfc9550207e4ad3859b17 over 38 deposits in the following hour, which is the source of the widely reported ~$1.1M; that figure is post-slippage and is not used here. Nothing was recovered.
